records.description: Replace the random forest with LightGBM (learning rate 0.01, up to 2000 rounds), choosing the round count by early stopping (100 rounds) on a seeded 15% validation split of each training fold, then refitting on the full fold with that count.
Switch the Morgan fingerprint to the feature-invariant (FCFP-style) atom typing via GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen, keeping radius 2, 2048 bits, and the LightGBM model unchanged.

Replace the LightGBM model with an SVR on a precomputed Tanimoto (Jaccard) kernel over the binary Morgan fingerprints, C=5, epsilon=0.05, with the target standardized so epsilon is on a sensible scale.
Abort: the proposed swap from the random forest to LightGBM does not apply to the current file, and LightGBM already scored worse than the incumbent SVR in slot 0.
Append the 167-bit MACCS keys to the Morgan bits before the Tanimoto kernel, since the current script has no random forest to hstack into (the SVR on a Tanimoto kernel is now the model).
Abort: the spec's random-forest leaf-size and bootstrap tweak does not apply to the current SVR-on-Tanimoto incumbent.
Abort: the Extra-Trees idea assumes a RandomForestRegressor that the current train.py does not contain (it uses an SVR on a Tanimoto kernel), so there is nothing to swap.

Rank-normalize the training target (ranks mapped to (0,1) via (rank-0.5)/n) before the SVR fit, adapted to the current Tanimoto-SVR model since the spec's RandomForestRegressor no longer exists in train.py.

Rank-normalize the training target (ranks mapped to (0,1) via (rank-0.5)/n) before the SVR fit, adapted to the current Tanimoto-SVR model since the spec's RandomForestRegressor no longer exists in train.py.
Abort: winsorizing training targets was specified for a random forest that train.py no longer contains, and the rank-normalized target already removes the leverage of extreme values.
Abort: the proposed change adds max_depth=12 and min_samples_leaf=3 to a RandomForestRegressor, but the current train.py has no random forest. It uses an SVR on a precomputed Tanimoto kernel.
Stack a random forest, a Tanimoto kernel ridge model and LightGBM with non-negative least-squares weights fitted on 5-fold inner out-of-fold predictions, keeping the rank-normalized target.
Abort: the proposed random-forest plus LightGBM rank blend assumes a RandomForestRegressor that the current train.py does not contain, so no edit was made.
Replace the Tanimoto-kernel SVR with a RidgeCV model on standardized RDKit 2D descriptors (NaN/inf filled with training medians, clipped z-scores), keeping the rank-normalized target.

issues: No gaming found: no file or network access, no pasted answers, no use of test labels. The scaler is fit on the training rows only; the rank transform of y uses the training fold only.
No bug that makes the result meaningless. Huge descriptor values (e.g. Ipc) are clipped to ±1e6 and then to ±5 after scaling; the MLPs are seeded from `seed`.
Minor: MolFromSmiles is called again for every descriptor (slower, but correct). The tanimoto helper may now be unused.

Numbers match: the candidate's 0.55 is worse than the incumbent's 0.5308. Recomputed z ≈ -2.24 with sd_diff = 0.007*sqrt(1+1/2); the harness's -2.228 fits the incumbent mean being rounded. Reject is correct.

records.description: Replace the Tanimoto-kernel SVR with an averaged ensemble of three sklearn MLPRegressors (256,128 hidden units, alpha=1e-2, early stopping) trained on standardized RDKit descriptors concatenated with Morgan bits, keeping the rank-normalized target.
Switch Morgan featurization to count-based radius-2 2048-bin fingerprints, and make the Tanimoto kernel use squared norms so it stays a valid similarity on count vectors.
Switch Morgan featurization to count-based radius-2 2048-bin fingerprints, and make the Tanimoto kernel use squared norms so it stays a valid similarity on count vectors.

Append standardized RDKit 2D descriptors to the model by averaging the Tanimoto kernel with an RBF kernel on the descriptors, since the current model is an SVR (not a random forest) and a binary-fingerprint Tanimoto kernel cannot take continuous features directly.
Replace the Morgan features with concatenated hashed atom-pair count (2048) and topological-torsion count (1024) fingerprints in the Tanimoto/RBF kernel model.

The job timed out because RDKit's full Descriptors.descList (about 210 descriptors) was recomputed from scratch for every molecule in each of the 15 fits; caching the per-molecule descriptor rows by SMILES makes each molecule compute once per job, leaving the model unchanged.

Weight each training molecule by the inverse frequency of its Murcko scaffold (mean-normalized to 1) and pass these as sample_weight to the SVR fit, since the random forest the spec names is no longer in train.py.
Abort: the spec's premise (swapping a random forest for CatBoost on Morgan bits) does not match the current train.py, which has no forest and uses a Tanimoto+descriptor kernel SVR.
Abort: log-transforming the target is a no-op here because the target is already rank-normalized, and the spec's random forest is no longer in train.py.
Replace the SVR head with sklearn KernelRidge (precomputed kernel, alpha=0.3) on the current mixed kernel, fitting mean-centred rank targets and adding the mean back to predictions.
Abort: the Huber-loss LightGBM idea does not fit the current train.py, which has no LightGBM model.
Seed-averaged bagging of the model was considered but not run, because the current train.py has no random forest or LightGBM to bag and its SVR head is deterministic.

Add a min-max (generalized Jaccard) kernel on unfolded radius-2 Morgan count fingerprints as a third term in the averaged kernel, alongside the Tanimoto bit kernel and the RBF descriptor kernel, keeping SVR and the rank target unchanged.

Before building the descriptor RBF kernel, keep only the 60 standardized RDKit descriptors with the largest absolute Spearman correlation to the training target (computed on training molecules only), with gamma = 1/60 on the selected columns.

Replace the fixed 0.5/0.5 kernel mix with closed-form kernel-target-alignment weights (centered Gram matrices, clipped and normalized to sum to 1) computed on the training fold, keeping SVR C=5 and epsilon=0.05.

Average 10 SVRs, each using the full Morgan-Tanimoto kernel mixed with an RBF kernel on its own seeded random 50% subset of the standardized RDKit descriptors, to reduce dependence on any one descriptor combination.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted answers. Only train_y is used, to build the ranking pairs, and test predictions are K_test @ alpha.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The new model is a pairwise-hinge ranking model on the same mixed kernel (Tanimoto plus RBF), fitted with L-BFGS. I checked the analytic gradient: the hinge part is K @ g_f with the coef sign handled correctly, and the regulariser part 2*lam*K@a is right because K is symmetric. Tied pairs are excluded, and pair sampling uses the seed argument. Memory and time look fine (about 15.5k pairs and n of about 776 per fold).

The numbers back the decision. The candidate's loss is 0.5957 against the incumbent's 0.4830, so it is about 0.113 worse. The difference is far beyond the noise, and rejecting it is right. A likely cause is that the hinge part is only a weak signal with lam=0.01 on an unnormalised kernel. Whatever the cause, it is a real result, not an artifact.

Recomputing z with one run each and noise sd 0.0070 gives z = (0.4830-0.5957)/(0.0070*sqrt(2)) ≈ -11.38. The harness reported -11.332. The small gap probably comes from a slightly different sd estimate or from how the values were adjusted, and it does not change the conclusion.
Each side has only one run. The gap is so large that this does not matter here.

records.description: Replace the SVR head with a kernel RankSVM model: f = K @ alpha, trained with a sampled pairwise hinge loss (about 20 pairs per molecule, seeded) plus 0.01 * alpha^T K alpha, minimized by L-BFGS with an analytic gradient, and predicted as K_test @ alpha.

Replace the single radius-2 Morgan Tanimoto kernel with the mean of Tanimoto kernels over radius 1, 2 and 3 fingerprints (2048 bits each), keeping the descriptor RBF kernel, the 0.5 mix, and the SVR and rank target unchanged.
Adds a Tanimoto kernel on RDKit path-based fingerprints (maxPath=6, 2048 bits) and averages it equally with the Morgan-Tanimoto and descriptor-RBF kernels, K = (K_morgan + K_desc + K_path) / 3.

Replace the SVR head with a Laplacian-regularized transductive solve: a 0.5 Tanimoto/descriptor-RBF kernel over train plus test molecules, a symmetric 7-NN graph with kernel-value weights, and f = (S + 0.5 L)^-1 S y, where test predictions are read from f.

Weight each standardized RDKit descriptor column by its absolute Spearman correlation with the rank-normalized training target (computed on the training fold, mean-normalized to 1, applied as sqrt(w) column scaling) and set the descriptor RBF gamma to 1/sum(w), leaving the Tanimoto kernel and 0.5/0.5 mix unchanged.

Fit a ridge prior (alpha=10) on seven standardized physchem descriptors to the rank-normalized target, then fit the Tanimoto/descriptor-kernel SVR to the residual and add the ridge prediction back at test time.

Fit a ridge prior (alpha=10) on seven standardized physchem descriptors to the rank-normalized target, then fit the Tanimoto/descriptor-kernel SVR to the residual and add the ridge prediction back at test time.
Add a Gobbi 2D pharmacophore Tanimoto kernel (hashed to 4096 bins) and average it equally with the Morgan-Tanimoto and descriptor-RBF kernels, leaving the SVR and rank target unchanged.

issues: No measurement circumvention: the new Gobbi 2D pharmacophore features are derived from SMILES only; pharm(test_smiles) is used solely as test-side features in the test-vs-train kernel. No test labels, file, or network access.

No meaningfulness-breaking bug: folding sparse pharmacophore bits with modulo 4096 causes some bit collisions but is valid; Tanimoto on 0/1 float arrays is valid; the mean of three valid kernels remains a valid kernel.
Gain is small and rests on 2 candidate runs vs 1 incumbent run, so it is within noise; the provisional reject is consistent with the numbers.
Minor: the extra per-molecule pharmacophore generation adds runtime; worth confirming the job still fits the 10-minute limit for 15 fits.

records.description: Add a Gobbi 2D pharmacophore Tanimoto kernel (hashed to 4096 bins) and average it equally with the Morgan-Tanimoto and descriptor-RBF kernels, leaving the SVR and rank target unchanged.

Append RDKit's 192-value CalcAUTOCORR2D autocorrelation descriptors (Moreau-Broto-type, Gasteiger-charge and atomic-property weighted) to the existing RDKit descriptor block so they pass through the unchanged constant-column filter, standardization, clipping and RBF descriptor kernel.

Adds a radius-2 2048-bit Morgan Tanimoto kernel on side-chain-only fragments (Murcko scaffold atoms removed via RWMol) and averages it equally with the full-molecule Tanimoto and descriptor RBF kernels, keeping the same SVR.

Replace the RBF descriptor kernel with a Laplacian kernel exp(-gamma * L1 distance) on the standardized descriptors, computed in row chunks, keeping the Tanimoto average, gamma=1/n_features, and SVR(C=5, epsilon=0.05).

Average three SVRs, each on the Morgan-Tanimoto/descriptor-RBF kernel mix but with the RDKit descriptors scaled differently (z-score with clipping, robust median/IQR, or rank-Gaussian fitted on the training fold), and average their test predictions after converting each to within-test ranks.

After the SVR predicts the test molecules, blend each prediction 0.7/0.3 with the mean prediction of its test-set neighbours (Tanimoto >= 0.5, diagonal excluded, row-normalized), leaving molecules with no neighbours unchanged; the training pipeline is untouched.

Weight each standardized RDKit descriptor by its absolute Spearman correlation with the training target (floored at 0.05, computed on the training fold only), scale the descriptor columns by these weights, and set the RBF gamma to 1/sum(w^2), leaving the Morgan-Tanimoto kernel and SVR settings unchanged.

Replace the z-score-and-clip step on the standardized RDKit descriptor matrix with a per-column normal-quantile transform fitted on the training fold (training ranks mapped via (rank-0.5)/n and norm.ppf; test values mapped by np.interp over the sorted training values), leaving the Morgan Tanimoto kernel, the gamma setting and the SVR unchanged.

issues: No sign of a measurement workaround. There is no file or network access, no pasted answers, and no use of test labels. The IDF is computed from the train and test fingerprints together, which uses the test SMILES but not their labels. fit_predict receives those SMILES as inputs, so this is legitimate transductive use. Still, it makes the predictions depend on what else is in the test batch, and the final scoring on held-out molecules will use a different test batch.

The Tanimoto change is correct. Once A = x*sqrt(idf), A@B.T gives the idf-weighted intersection. For binary fingerprints, the squared row sums give the idf-weighted bit counts. That makes the result a proper weighted Tanimoto. Without the squaring, the scaled vectors would give the wrong norms.

Not checked: the rest of train.py is not visible. If tanimoto is also called somewhere on unscaled inputs, or if the scaled X goes to a model that expects binary bits, this change also affects that path. That would not invalidate the result.

Recomputed z = (0.4830 - 0.4826) / (0.0070 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/1)) ≈ 0.04, which matches the reported 0.041. A gain of 0.0004 is well within the noise (sd 0.0070), so rejecting it is consistent with the numbers. The added code is also not justified by such a small gain.

records.description: Weight each radius-2 2048-bit Morgan bit by its transductive IDF (sqrt-scaled columns) so the Tanimoto kernel becomes IDF-weighted, keeping the 0.5/0.5 mix with the descriptor RBF kernel and the SVR head unchanged.

Appends about 15 hand-written ionization SMARTS counts (acids, tetrazole, acyl sulfonamide, aliphatic amines, amidine/guanidine, basic aromatic N, phenol, sulfonic/phosphonic acid, quaternary N, aniline) to the RDKit descriptor matrix, so they go through the same standardization, clipping and descriptor RBF kernel.

Append a 13-pattern SMARTS soft-spot count block (benzylic C-H, N-methyl/ethyl, O-methyl, aromatic CH, thioether, furan, thiophene, methylenedioxy, tertiary C-H, morpholine, N-methyl aromatic, ester alkyl) to the RDKit descriptor matrix before standardization and the RBF descriptor kernel, leaving the Tanimoto part, 0.5/0.5 mix and SVR unchanged.

Add an ARDRegression (default priors, max_iter=300) on the standardized, clipped RDKit descriptors, fit to the rank-normalized target, and output 0.7 times the SVR test-set rank plus 0.3 times the ARD test-set rank.

memo: Helped: changing model family (LightGBM 0.5726, Tanimoto-kernel SVR 0.5491, from 0.6103 start), rank-normalizing the target (0.5310/0.5307, replicated), and above all averaging the Tanimoto kernel with an RDKit 2D descriptor RBF kernel (0.4830, incumbent). Did not help: FCFP (0.5877), MACCS (0.5421), stacking (0.5558), MLP ensemble (0.5500), descriptor-only ridge (0.5328), 60-descriptor subset (0.4973), autocorrelation descriptors (0.5057), RankSVM (0.5957), Laplacian solve (0.5716). Within noise (sd about 0.0070): scaffold weighting 0.4803, KernelRidge 0.4822, descriptor weighting 0.4824, extra kernels (0.4854-0.4860). Gobbi kernel (0.4680/0.4791) and ridge prior (0.4711/0.4728) were borderline gains that did not hold up on replication. Kernels look plateaued near 0.48. Next: tune SVR C, epsilon and descriptor gamma; try a GP; try quantile-transformed descriptors; maybe combine Gobbi with the ridge prior. Read train.py first, since many edits aborted by assuming a random forest or LightGBM. Replicate gains under 0.01.

incumbent.description: Append standardized RDKit 2D descriptors to the model by averaging the Tanimoto kernel with an RBF kernel on the descriptors, since the current model is an SVR (not a random forest) and a binary-fingerprint Tanimoto kernel cannot take continuous features directly.

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, replace train_y with its rank-normalized version (scipy.stats.rankdata divided by n, mapped to (0,1)) before fitting the same RandomForestRegressor. Predictions are then ranks on the training scale, which directly targets the Spearman metric. Return the model's predictions unchanged.
backlog.title: Rank-transform the training target

backlog.spec: Fit the RandomForestRegressor on log(train_y) when all training values are positive (use log1p with a shift by the minimum otherwise), and invert the transform on the test predictions with exp or expm1 minus the shift. This compresses the right-skewed clearance tail so the forest is not dominated by a few large values.
backlog.title: Log-transform the target

backlog.spec: Change featurize to use the count-based Morgan fingerprint (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) at radius 2 with 2048 bins, so each feature records how many times an atom environment occurs rather than only whether it occurs. Keep the rest of the pipeline identical.
backlog.title: Morgan count fingerprints instead of bits

backlog.spec: Concatenate the full RDKit Descriptors.descList values (computed per molecule, with NaN and inf replaced by 0 and values clipped to a finite range) to the Morgan bit vector before fitting the random forest. Physicochemical properties such as logP, TPSA and molecular weight are known drivers of hepatic clearance and are missing from pure fingerprints.
backlog.title: Append RDKit 2D physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Build a 167-bit MACCS keys fingerprint with rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys for each molecule and hstack it with the Morgan bits as the feature matrix for the random forest. The MACCS keys capture coarse functional-group presence that a radius-2 Morgan hash can miss.
backlog.title: Add MACCS structural keys

backlog.spec: Use the feature-invariant Morgan generator (GetMorganGenerator with an atom invariant generator from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen) so atoms are typed by pharmacophoric role (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) rather than element identity. Keep radius 2 and 2048 bits and leave the model unchanged.
backlog.title: Feature-invariant (FCFP-style) Morgan fingerprint

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan features with the concatenation of hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (GetAtomPairGenerator, 2048 bits) and topological-torsion count fingerprints (GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, 1024 bits). These encode longer-range topology than circular environments and give the forest a different view of the same molecules.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and topological-torsion fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForestRegressor with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor on the same Morgan bit features, using around 600 trees, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, min_child_samples 10, and random_state=seed. Boosting often beats bagging on fingerprint regression when data is small.
backlog.title: Gradient-boosted trees with LightGBM

backlog.spec: Swap the forest for catboost.CatBoostRegressor with about 800 iterations, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, l2_leaf_reg 3, verbose disabled and random_seed=seed, trained on the Morgan bit matrix. CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees are more resistant to overfitting on a 970-molecule set.
backlog.title: CatBoost regressor on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (Jaccard) similarity matrix between binary Morgan fingerprints of train and test molecules (K = A·B / (|A| + |B| − A·B) using numpy), then fit sklearn SVR with kernel='precomputed' and C around 5, epsilon 0.05. Tanimoto kernels are the standard similarity measure for chemical activity regression.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression

backlog.spec: Use the same precomputed Tanimoto kernel on Morgan bits and fit sklearn KernelRidge with kernel='precomputed' and alpha around 0.3, centering train_y by its mean before fitting and adding the mean back to test predictions. Kernel ridge gives smooth similarity-weighted predictions with a closed form and no randomness.
backlog.title: Gaussian process / kernel ridge with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: For each test molecule compute Tanimoto similarity to all training molecules, keep the k=10 most similar training molecules, and predict the average of their train_y weighted by similarity raised to the power 3. This is a simple local model that is naturally robust to unseen scaffolds when similarity is low.
backlog.title: Similarity-weighted k-nearest-neighbour regression

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with sklearn ExtraTreesRegressor using the same n_estimators, max_features=0.3 and random_state=seed on the Morgan bit matrix. Extra-Trees picks split thresholds at random, which smooths predictions and often generalises better across unseen scaffolds on small noisy datasets.
backlog.title: Extra-Trees regressor

backlog.spec: Fit both the existing RandomForestRegressor and a LightGBM regressor (modest settings, random_state=seed) on the same features, convert each model's test predictions to ranks, and return the equal-weight average of the two rank vectors scaled to [0,1]. Averaging diverse learners usually improves rank correlation.
backlog.title: Blend of random forest and gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, run 5-fold inner cross-validation on the training molecules to produce out-of-fold predictions from a random forest, a Tanimoto-kernel ridge model and a LightGBM model. Fit a non-negative linear regression (scipy.optimize.nnls or sklearn LinearRegression with positive=True) on those out-of-fold predictions, then refit the base models on all training data and apply the learned weights to the test predictions.
backlog.title: Stacking with a linear meta-learner

backlog.spec: Compute RDKit 2D descriptors for each molecule, replace NaN and infinite values with the training median, standardize with a scaler fit on training data only, and fit sklearn RidgeCV with alphas logspaced from 1e-2 to 1e3. A regularized linear model on physicochemical descriptors gives a different inductive bias that can be blended later.
backlog.title: Ridge regression on standardized descriptors

backlog.spec: Standardize the concatenated RDKit descriptors and Morgan bits (scaler fit on training data), then fit sklearn MLPRegressor with hidden_layer_sizes=(256,128), alpha=1e-2 (L2 penalty), early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.15, max_iter 500, and random_state=seed. Averaging several seeds of the network reduces its variance.
backlog.title: Small MLP on descriptors and fingerprints

backlog.spec: Keep RandomForestRegressor but cap tree depth with max_depth=12 and raise min_samples_leaf to 3. Restricting tree complexity smooths the predicted values and reduces overfitting to specific skeleton clusters in the training folds.
backlog.title: Random forest with shallower trees

backlog.spec: Set RandomForestRegressor min_samples_leaf to 5 and max_samples to 0.7 with bootstrap=True. Larger leaves average more molecules per prediction and subsampling decorrelates trees, both of which reduce variance on a few hundred to one thousand noisy measurements.
backlog.title: Larger minimum leaf size and bootstrap sampling tweaks

backlog.spec: Use LightGBM with objective='huber' (alpha set to the 90th percentile of absolute residuals of the training targets) on the Morgan bit features. Huber loss limits the influence of outlier clearance measurements, which otherwise pull the fitted trees toward extreme values.
backlog.title: Huber loss in gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Before fitting, clip train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles computed on the training fold only, then fit the existing random forest on the clipped values. Removing extreme measurement noise reduces leverage of a few values on the learned partition structure.
backlog.title: Winsorize extreme training targets

backlog.spec: Compute Murcko scaffolds for training molecules and weight each sample by the inverse of its scaffold's frequency (normalized to mean 1) and pass these as sample_weight to the random forest fit. Over-represented scaffolds then do not dominate the trees, which better matches the unseen-scaffold test condition.
backlog.title: Scaffold-density sample weighting

backlog.spec: After featurizing the training set, drop any Morgan bit that is set in fewer than 2 or more than 98 percent of training molecules, applying the same column mask to the test set. Removing uninformative sparse columns reduces noise and speeds up the random forest's feature sampling.
backlog.title: Remove near-constant fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Increase N_TREES from 300 to 1000 and keep the other random forest settings. More trees lower the variance of the averaged prediction, which should marginally improve the stability of rank correlation across folds at the cost of runtime that stays well within the job limit.
backlog.title: Larger forest with more trees

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM with a small learning rate (0.01) and a large maximum number of trees (2000), using an internal validation split of 15 percent of the training fold with early_stopping(100) to choose the number of boosting rounds, then refit on the full training fold with that round count. Early stopping keeps the boosting schedule from overfitting.
backlog.title: Gradient boosting with learning-rate and tree-count schedule

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train the random forest (or LightGBM) three times with seeds derived from the given seed (seed, seed+1, seed+2) and average their test predictions. Averaging independent fits reduces run-to-run variance of the final predictions without changing the model family.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged bagging of the whole model

backlog.spec: Train lightgbm.LGBMRanker with objective='lambdarank' on Morgan bit features, using a single query group containing all training molecules and integer relevance labels obtained by binning train_y into 10 quantile levels. Directly optimizing pairwise order matches the Spearman-based loss better than squared error.
backlog.title: Pairwise ranking objective with LightGBM

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, build the fingerprint kernel as the mean of Tanimoto kernels over three Morgan fingerprints computed at radius 1, 2 and 3 (2048 bits each), instead of the single radius-2 Tanimoto matrix. Keep the descriptor RBF kernel and the 0.5 mixing as they are: K = 0.5 * (mean_r tanimoto_r + rbf). Compute the train-train and test-test kernels the same way. Leave SVR(C=5, epsilon=0.05) and the rank target unchanged. The change is confined to featurize calls and the K_train/K_test lines.
backlog.title: Multi-radius Tanimoto kernel average

backlog.spec: Before any featurization, preprocess each SMILES: parse with RDKit, keep only the largest covalently connected fragment (strip salts and counterions), and neutralize charges where possible. Pass useChirality=True to the Morgan generator so stereo centres enter the fingerprint. Apply the same preprocessing to train and test SMILES, including inside descriptors(). Everything else in the pipeline stays the same. Guard against None from MolFromSmiles by falling back to the raw string.
backlog.title: Salt-stripped, chirality-aware canonicalization

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed gamma = 1/n_features in the descriptor RBF kernel with a choice among multipliers {0.25, 1, 4} times 1/n_features. Select the multiplier inside fit_predict with a 3-fold inner split of the training molecules, scoring each by Spearman correlation between predicted and true training values in the held-out inner folds. Then refit on all training molecules with the chosen gamma and predict the test molecules. Use the seed argument for the inner split.
backlog.title: Descriptor-kernel gamma chosen by inner CV

backlog.spec: Swap the descriptor kernel from RBF (Gaussian in squared Euclidean distance) to a Laplacian kernel exp(-gamma * L1 distance), with L1 distance computed as sum of absolute differences over the standardized, clipped descriptor columns. Keep gamma = 1/n_features, keep the Tanimoto term and the 0.5 average, and keep SVR(C=5, epsilon=0.05) on the rank target. Compute the pairwise L1 distances with broadcasting in chunks to stay within the 6 GB memory limit.
backlog.title: Laplacian kernel on standardized descriptors

backlog.spec: Generalize the fixed 0.5 average to K = w * tanimoto + (1 - w) * rbf_descriptor, with w chosen from {0.3, 0.5, 0.7}. Pick w inside fit_predict by a 3-fold inner split on the training molecules, scoring each choice by the Spearman correlation of held-out predictions with the rank target. Refit on all training molecules with the chosen w and predict the test set. Use the seed argument for the inner split.
backlog.title: Kernel mixing weight selected by inner CV

backlog.spec: Keep the mixed kernel exactly as in the incumbent. Inside fit_predict, grid-search SVR hyperparameters over C in {1, 5, 20} and epsilon in {0.02, 0.05, 0.1} using a 3-fold inner split of the training molecules, scoring by Spearman correlation on held-out inner folds. Refit SVR on all training molecules with the best pair and return test predictions. Use the seed argument for the inner split. Standardize the rank target as before.
backlog.title: SVR C and epsilon grid via inner validation

backlog.spec: Before the descriptor RBF kernel is built, keep only the k standardized RDKit descriptors whose absolute Spearman correlation with the training target is largest, with k = 60. Compute the correlations inside fit_predict on the training molecules only, so no test information leaks in. Build the RBF kernel with gamma = 1/k on the selected columns. Keep the Tanimoto term, the 0.5 average, and SVR(C=5, epsilon=0.05) unchanged.
backlog.title: Top-k descriptor selection by target correlation

backlog.spec: Add a third kernel term to the mix: a min-max kernel on Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bins, unfolded counts). For two count vectors a and b, the kernel is sum_i min(a_i, b_i) / sum_i max(a_i, b_i), computed with broadcasting in chunks to respect memory. The combined kernel is (tanimoto_bits + minmax_counts + rbf_descriptor) / 3. Keep SVR(C=5, epsilon=0.05) and the rank target unchanged.
backlog.title: Min-max (generalized Jaccard) count kernel in the mix

backlog.spec: After removing near-constant descriptors, drop redundant ones before standardization. Compute the Pearson correlation matrix of the training-set descriptor columns, and for each pair with absolute correlation above 0.95, drop the column with the higher mean absolute correlation to the others. Apply the same column selection to test descriptors. Then standardize, clip to [-5, 5], and build the RBF kernel with gamma = 1/n_kept. Everything else stays as in the incumbent.
backlog.title: Redundant-descriptor pruning by correlation

backlog.spec: Instead of a single SVR, fit three SVR models on the same mixed kernel with C in {1, 5, 20} and epsilon = 0.05. Convert each model's test predictions to ranks within the test set, then average the three rank vectors and return the average as the prediction. The ensemble has no inner validation and no extra randomness, so the seed argument is unused. Keep the mixed kernel and rank target unchanged.
backlog.title: Ensemble of SVRs over the C grid with averaged ranks

backlog.spec: Add a third kernel built from RDKit's Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprints (rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Gobbi.Generate / Gobbi_Pharm2D.factory with a SigFactory, converted to a 0/1 numpy vector, or a fixed-size hash of the bit vector). Compute its Tanimoto kernel on train and test, then set the final kernel to the equal-weight average of the existing Morgan-Tanimoto kernel, the descriptor RBF kernel, and this pharmacophore Tanimoto kernel: K = (K_morgan + K_desc + K_pharm) / 3. Leave the SVR (C=5, epsilon=0.05) and the rank-target transform unchanged.
backlog.title: Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprint kernel in the mix

backlog.spec: Add a Tanimoto kernel on RDKit's topological path fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetRDKitFPGenerator with maxPath=6, fpSize=2048, as a 0/1 array). Keep the existing Morgan-Tanimoto and descriptor RBF kernels and average all three equally: K = (K_morgan + K_desc + K_path) / 3. Nothing else changes, so the only effect tested is the added path-based similarity.
backlog.title: RDKit path-based fingerprint kernel in the mix

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 0.5/0.5 mix of the Morgan-Tanimoto kernel and the descriptor RBF kernel with weights chosen in closed form on the training fold, without any CV. Build the two training Gram matrices, center each one (H K H, H = I - 11^T/n), and set w_k proportional to the centered alignment <Kc_k, yy^T>_F / ||Kc_k||_F, where y is the standardized rank target. Clip negative weights to zero, normalize so the weights sum to 1, and use K = w1*K_morgan + w2*K_desc for both train and test Gram matrices. Keep SVR C=5, epsilon=0.05.
backlog.title: Kernel-target-alignment learned mixing weights

backlog.spec: Replace the SVR head with a kernel RankSVM-style model that optimizes pairwise order directly, since the score is Spearman-based. Using the precomputed mixed kernel K (existing Tanimoto + descriptor RBF average), represent the function as f = K @ alpha. Sample about 20 pairs (i, j) per training molecule with y_i != y_j (use the seed), and minimize the mean hinge loss max(0, 1 - sign(y_i - y_j)(f_i - f_j)) plus lambda * alpha^T K alpha with L-BFGS (scipy.optimize.minimize, analytic gradient). Predict on test as K_test @ alpha. Use lambda around 0.01 and check it by a single run.
backlog.title: Kernel pairwise ranking model instead of SVR

backlog.spec: Use the unlabelled test molecules in a self-training round inside fit_predict. First fit the current SVR on the training fold and predict the test set. Take the 30% of test molecules whose predictions are closest to the training-set extremes or whose SVR decision is most confident (for example, the lowest and highest 15% of predicted values) and add them to the training set with their predicted rank-scale targets, at a weight of 0.5 if sample weights are supported (or simply as-is). Refit the SVR on the augmented set with the same kernel and hyperparameters, and return its predictions for the test set. This is one retraining pass; do not iterate further.
backlog.title: Transductive self-training with test pseudo-labels

backlog.spec: After fitting the SVR on the mixed kernel, compute out-of-fold residuals on the training set with a 5-fold inner split (seeded). Then, for each test molecule, find its k=5 most similar training molecules by Morgan Tanimoto and add the similarity-weighted mean of their inner-fold residuals, scaled by 0.5, to the SVR prediction. This corrects local bias the global kernel model leaves behind. Keep the mixed kernel, SVR C=5, epsilon=0.05, and the rank target otherwise unchanged.
backlog.title: Residual kNN correction on top of the SVR

backlog.spec: Before building the descriptor RBF kernel, weight each standardized RDKit descriptor by its absolute Spearman correlation with the training target, computed on the training fold only. Scale each standardized descriptor column by w_j = |rho_j| / max_k |rho_k| (floored at 0.05), so that the RBF distance emphasises descriptors that track clearance. Compute the RBF with gamma = 1/(sum of w_j^2) to keep the kernel width sensible. Leave the Morgan-Tanimoto half of the mix and the SVR settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Supervised descriptor weighting by train-fold correlation

backlog.spec: Build 10 SVR models, each using a different random subset of 50% of the standardized RDKit descriptor columns (drawn with the seed) for the descriptor RBF half of the mixed kernel. Each model uses the full Morgan-Tanimoto kernel plus its own subspace RBF kernel, with the same SVR settings (C=5, epsilon=0.05). Average the 10 predicted rank-scale values for the test set. This reduces dependence on any single descriptor combination.
backlog.title: Random-subspace ensemble of descriptor kernels

backlog.spec: Before fitting the SVR, smooth the rank-normalized training target over the training set itself. For each training molecule, compute the mean rank-target of its k=3 most similar other training molecules by Morgan Tanimoto (excluding itself), and set the fitted target to 0.8 * own rank-target + 0.2 * that neighbour mean. The SVR is then fit on these smoothed targets and predicts test molecules as before. This regularises noisy labels for close analogues without changing the test-time model.
backlog.title: Target smoothing over nearest training neighbours

backlog.spec: Fit a ridge regression (alpha=10) on a small set of standardized physchem descriptors (RDKit MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3) on the rank-normalized training target. Subtract this linear prior from the training target, fit the Tanimoto/descriptor-kernel SVR to the residual, and at prediction time add the ridge prior back to the SVR output for test molecules. The prior encodes known lipophilicity and polarity trends in clearance so the kernel only has to model what is left over. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Linear physicochemical prior fitted before the SVR

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit the existing Tanimoto+descriptor SVR on all training molecules. Compute each training molecule's absolute out-of-fold-free residual (|y - prediction| on the training set). Then run a schedule of 3 stages: keep the 100%, 85%, then 70% of training molecules with the smallest residuals, refitting the SVR on the kept subset each stage (same kernel, C and epsilon). Predict test molecules with the final stage model. Only the training subset changes; the kernel and target transform stay as they are.
backlog.title: Self-paced curriculum for the SVR

backlog.spec: Replace the SVR head with kernel ridge regression fitted by iteratively reweighted least squares under a Huber loss. Start with alpha = solve(K + lam*I, y) using the current combined kernel K and the rank-normalized target, lam = 0.3. Each of about 10 iterations computes residuals r = y - K@alpha on the training set, sets weights w_i = min(1, delta/|r_i|) with delta = 0.2 (in standardized target units), and solves the weighted system (W K + lam*I) alpha = W y. Predict with K_test @ alpha. Robust weighting limits the influence of outlying clearance values.
backlog.title: Huber-loss kernel ridge via IRLS

backlog.spec: Use the test molecules as unlabeled nodes. Build the combined kernel K over train plus test molecules (same Tanimoto plus descriptor RBF mix). Form a symmetric kNN graph (k = 7, weights = kernel values) over all molecules and its normalized Laplacian L. Solve for f over all nodes that minimizes sum over training nodes of (f_i - y_i)^2 plus gamma * f^T L f, with gamma = 0.5, by a single linear solve. Predict the test entries of f. This smooths predictions over the joint chemical neighbourhood graph without any pseudo-labels being fed back.
backlog.title: Laplacian-regularized transductive kernel regression

backlog.spec: Fit the current SVR to the rank-normalized target. Compute training residuals r = y - f(train) using in-sample predictions. Fit a second kernel model (kernel ridge, lam = 1.0, same combined kernel) to r. Repeat for 4 rounds. Each round adds its output with a shrinkage factor that decays on a schedule: nu_m = 0.5 * 0.7**m for round m. The final prediction is the SVR output plus the sum of the shrunken correction models evaluated on test molecules. Keep the number of rounds small so the in-sample residuals do not vanish.
backlog.title: Residual boosting of kernel models with shrinkage schedule

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, draw 20 bootstrap-free random subsets of the training molecules, each containing 70% of them, using a numpy RandomState seeded from the seed argument. Fit the existing combined-kernel SVR on each subset (index the precomputed kernel matrix, so no kernel is recomputed). Predict the held-out test molecules with each model, convert each set of predictions to ranks, and return the mean rank per test molecule rescaled to (0, 1). Averaging over subsets reduces variance from any single training draw.
backlog.title: Bagged SVRs on random 70% subsamples with rank averaging

backlog.spec: Before fitting, create 2*n_train virtual training examples. Each virtual example is a convex combination of two training molecules with weight lam drawn from Beta(0.4, 0.4) per example (seeded from the seed argument). Its target is the same convex combination of their rank-normalized targets. Because the SVR uses a precomputed kernel, build the virtual kernel rows directly: K_virtual(i,j) = lam*K(a,j)+(1-lam)*K(b,j), and the virtual-to-virtual block is built the same way from the original kernel matrix. Fit the SVR on the augmented set and predict test molecules with the ordinary test kernel row.
backlog.title: Kernel mixup as regularization

backlog.spec: Replace the hand-set 0.5/0.5 kernel mix and fixed gamma with values chosen by GP marginal likelihood. Build the Tanimoto kernel Kt and the descriptor RBF kernel Kd once for the training set. For a grid of mixing weights w in {0.2, 0.35, 0.5, 0.65, 0.8} and noise levels s2 in {0.1, 0.3, 1.0}, compute the log marginal likelihood of standardized targets under K = w*Kt + (1-w)*Kd + s2*I (Cholesky via numpy.linalg). Choose the pair with the highest likelihood, then predict the test molecules with the GP posterior mean. Only the hyperparameter selection is new; the model is still kernel regression.
backlog.title: Type-II maximum likelihood for kernel hyperparameters

backlog.spec: Replace the kernel model with a small graph neural network written in numpy. Each molecule becomes an atom graph with atom features (element one-hot, degree, aromaticity, H count, ring membership, formal charge; about 30 dims) and the bond adjacency. Run 3 rounds of message passing, h <- tanh(W1 h + A h W2), with hidden size 32, then sum-pool atoms to a 32-dim vector and apply a linear readout. Train by full-batch Adam (learning rate 0.01, weight decay 1e-4, 300 epochs) on the rank-normalized target with MSE loss. Use the backward pass written by hand, or a finite-difference check on a tiny batch. Average 3 models with different initializations from the seed argument.
backlog.title: Small message-passing neural network in numpy

backlog.spec: Extend the descriptor block with RDKit 2D autocorrelation descriptors, computed per molecule with rdMolDescriptors.CalcAUTOCORR2D (length 192, gasteiger charge and atomic-property weighted) plus the Moreau-Broto autocorrelations. Concatenate these with the existing RDKit descriptors, drop near-constant columns, standardize on the training set, clip to [-5, 5], and feed the result into the existing RBF descriptor kernel. Leave the Tanimoto kernel and the 0.5/0.5 mix unchanged. Autocorrelation descriptors encode topological pharmacophore spacing that the Morgan bits do not capture directly.
backlog.title: 2D autocorrelation descriptors added to the descriptor kernel

backlog.spec: Before building the descriptor RBF kernel, weight each standardized RDKit descriptor column by the absolute Spearman correlation between that column and the rank-normalized training target, computed only on the training fold (w_j = |rho_j|, rescaled so the weights have mean 1, then column-scaled by sqrt(w_j)). Then build the RBF kernel with gamma = 1/(sum of w_j) instead of 1/D. The fingerprint Tanimoto kernel and the 0.5/0.5 mix stay the same. This biases the descriptor similarity toward the properties that actually track clearance, without dropping any columns.
backlog.title: Kernel SVR with correlation-weighted descriptor columns

backlog.spec: Keep the rest of fit_predict unchanged, but replace the Tanimoto term in the mixed kernel with a sharpened version: T_sharp = tanimoto(X, X) ** P, with P = 3.0 (also apply to the test-vs-train block). The mixed kernel is then K = 0.5 * (T_sharp + rbf(D, D, gamma)) and the SVR is fit on it as before. Sharpening makes near neighbours dominate and far pairs nearly zero, which may suit scaffold-held-out splits. Use the seed argument nowhere new; no other settings change.
backlog.title: Sharpened Tanimoto kernel via power transform

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace the z-score and clip step on the RDKit descriptor matrix D (and Dt) with a rank-based Gaussian transform fitted on the training fold only. For each kept column, map training values to their empirical quantiles in (0,1) with (rank - 0.5)/n, convert with scipy.stats.norm.ppf, and map test values by interpolating over the sorted training values (np.interp, clamped at the ends). Then compute gamma = 1/number_of_columns and build the RBF descriptor kernel as before. Leave the Morgan Tanimoto part and the SVR settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Normal-quantile descriptor transform instead of z-score clipping

backlog.spec: Add a small block of about 15 hand-written SMARTS counts that capture ionization, which drives hepatic clearance and logD: carboxylic acid, tetrazole, acyl sulfonamide, aliphatic primary/secondary/tertiary amine (not amide, not aniline), amidine/guanidine, pyridine-like basic N, phenol, sulfonic acid, quaternary N, and similar. Compute each count per molecule with Chem.MolFromSmiles and mol.GetSubstructMatches, append these counts to the standardized RDKit descriptor matrix D before the descriptor RBF kernel is built (same standardization and clipping), and keep everything else the same. Fit the training-fold statistics only.
backlog.title: Ionizable-group and charge-state count descriptors

backlog.spec: Build a second small feature block of 10 to 20 SMARTS patterns for common metabolic soft spots: benzylic CH2/CH3 next to aromatic rings, N-methyl or N-ethyl groups (N-dealkylation), O-methyl ethers (O-demethylation), unsubstituted para position on phenyl rings, thioethers, furans, thiophenes, methylenedioxy, and tertiary aliphatic C-H. Count matches per molecule with Chem.MolFromSmiles and GetSubstructMatches, then standardize these counts on the training fold and append them to the descriptor matrix before the RBF descriptor kernel. Keep the Tanimoto part, the mixing 0.5/0.5, and the SVR unchanged.
backlog.title: Cytochrome P450 soft-spot SMARTS count block

backlog.spec: For each molecule, embed one 3D conformer with rdkit.Chem.AllChem.EmbedMolecule using a fixed random seed derived from the seed argument (randomSeed=seed), with maxAttempts small and a fallback to 2D coordinates or zeros if embedding fails. Compute a short vector of shape descriptors: principal moments of inertia (normalized by their sum), radius of gyration, asphericity, eccentricity, plus rdMolDescriptors.CalcPBF and CalcNPR1/NPR2. Append this vector (about 8 columns) to the standardized RDKit descriptor matrix before the descriptor RBF kernel. Guard against the 10-minute job limit by using one conformer and no optimization step. Leave the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: 3D shape descriptors from a single ETKDG conformer

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, first fit the current SVR on all training molecules, then compute in-sample residuals between the standardized rank target and the model's fitted predictions on the training kernel. Discard the 10 percent of training molecules with the largest absolute residuals (keep the rest, preserving order), rebuild the training kernel submatrices for the retained rows only, and refit the SVR on the retained set. Predict test molecules with the refitted model. This is a one-pass robust trimming step that limits the effect of mislabelled or unusual measurements. Use the seed argument for nothing new; all other settings stay the same.
backlog.title: Trimmed refit that drops high-residual training molecules

backlog.spec: Build a second Morgan-style fingerprint on the molecule with the Murcko scaffold atoms removed, so that only substituent environments remain. For each molecule, compute MurckoDecompose or GetScaffold, delete the scaffold atoms with RWMol (keep the attachment-point dummy atoms out), then compute a radius-2 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint on the remaining fragments; molecules with no side chain get an all-zero vector. Add the Tanimoto kernel on this side-chain fingerprint as a third term: K = (1/3) * (Tanimoto_full + Tanimoto_sidechain + RBF_descriptor), with the same SVR. Because scaffold-held-out splits differ in ring systems, this term targets substituent effects that transfer across skeletons.
backlog.title: Side-chain fingerprint kernel that ignores the ring skeleton

backlog.spec: After fitting the SVR as now, compute its predictions on the training molecules (in-sample) and form residuals r = y_std - f_train. Fit a Ridge regression with alpha = 30 on the standardized RDKit descriptor matrix D (training fold only) to predict r. At prediction time, return the SVR test prediction plus 0.5 times the ridge prediction on Dt. The shrink factor 0.5 limits overfitting of the in-sample residuals. Keep the kernel, mixing weights, and SVR hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Residual ridge correction on standardized descriptors

backlog.spec: Run the full pipeline three times with three different scalings of the RDKit descriptor matrix: the current z-score with clipping, a robust scaling using median and IQR (clipped to plus or minus 5), and a rank-Gaussian transform fitted on the training fold. Each run builds its own descriptor RBF kernel (gamma = 1/number of columns), mixes it 0.5/0.5 with the shared Morgan Tanimoto kernel, and fits an SVR with C=5.0, epsilon=0.05 on the standardized rank target. Average the three test predictions after converting each to ranks within the test set, and return the averaged score. The Morgan featurization is computed once and shared across the three runs.
backlog.title: Ensemble of SVRs over three descriptor scalings with rank averaging

backlog.spec: After computing the SVR predictions for the test molecules, refine them using their similarity to each other. Compute the Tanimoto matrix among test molecules, Stest = tanimoto(Xt, Xt). For each test molecule, keep only neighbours with similarity at or above 0.5 (set others to zero), and form a row-normalized weight matrix W with the diagonal zeroed. Return final = 0.7 * base_prediction + 0.3 * (W @ base_prediction), where rows with no neighbours keep the base prediction. This uses the unlabelled test set only, adds no training data, and needs no extra fitting. Keep the training pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Transductive smoothing of test predictions over test-test similarity

backlog.spec: Keep the radius-2 2048-bit Morgan bits, but weight each bit by its inverse document frequency, idf_j = log((N+1)/(df_j+1)) + 1, where df_j is the number of molecules containing bit j in train plus test features (transductive, fingerprints only, no labels). Scale columns by sqrt(idf_j) before computing a weighted Tanimoto (A W B^T / (|A|_W + |B|_W - A W B^T)). Use this weighted Tanimoto in place of the unweighted one in the 0.5/0.5 mix with the descriptor RBF kernel, and leave the SVR head (C=5, epsilon=0.05, rank-normalized target) unchanged.
backlog.title: IDF-weighted Morgan Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Build a bag of character n-grams from each canonical SMILES string (n = 2 to 4, with counts, using a simple dict-based vocabulary fitted on train+test strings). Compute a normalized linear kernel on the L2-normalized count vectors, K_str = cosine similarity. Form the final kernel as an equal-weight average of the existing Tanimoto kernel, the descriptor RBF kernel and K_str, then fit the unchanged SVR on the precomputed matrix. This is a cheap, non-fingerprint view of the molecule's text that the graph-based kernels do not see.
backlog.title: SMILES character n-gram string kernel in the mix

backlog.spec: After the standardized and clipped RDKit descriptors are computed, fit sklearn NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis (n_components=16, max_iter=50, random_state=seed) on the training descriptors with the training labels binned into 5 quantile classes, as a supervised linear projection. Project train and test descriptors with the learned transform, then compute the RBF kernel with gamma = 1/n_components on the projected data. Keep the 0.5/0.5 mix with the Morgan Tanimoto kernel and the SVR head unchanged. The learned metric replaces the isotropic distance in the descriptor space.
backlog.title: Learned metric (NCA) on descriptors before the RBF kernel

backlog.spec: After fitting the SVR, for each test molecule take its k=30 most similar training molecules by the mixed kernel (k nearest in kernel space). On those neighbours, fit a small ridge regression (alpha=1.0) from the standardized descriptor vector to the SVR residual (true rank target minus the SVR in-sample prediction), weighted by kernel similarity. Add the local ridge prediction, scaled by 0.5, to the SVR output for that test molecule. This is a local linear correction, fit separately per test molecule, that adjusts the global kernel model where neighbours show a systematic descriptor trend.
backlog.title: Test-time locally weighted ridge correction

backlog.spec: Train the mixed-kernel SVR on 12 bootstrap resamples of the training set, where the resampling unit is the Murcko scaffold group and not the molecule: draw scaffold groups with replacement (or sample 80% of groups without replacement), and include all molecules of each drawn group. Each bag refits the SVR on the sub-kernel (index the precomputed train kernel). Predict the test molecules with each bag, convert each bag's predictions to ranks, and average the ranks. The bag seeds come from the seed argument. This matches the grouped structure of the evaluation rather than bagging single molecules.
backlog.title: Scaffold-level bagging of the SVR

backlog.spec: Replace the default Morgan atom invariants with a reduced set: for each atom, use only atomic number and heavy-atom degree (not hybridization, aromaticity, ring membership or H count) as the initial identifier. Use the Morgan generator with a custom atom-invariant list (for example via rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with a rdFingerprintGenerator.AdditionalOutput-free setup, or by computing the invariants with numpy and hashing them with a fixed function) at radius 2 and 2048 bits, binary. Keep the rest of the pipeline (Tanimoto kernel, descriptor RBF kernel, 0.5/0.5 mix, SVR head) unchanged. This coarser atom typing groups analogues that differ only in ring or hybridization details.
backlog.title: Reduced-invariant Morgan fingerprint (element and degree only)

backlog.spec: Replace gamma = 1/d in the descriptor RBF kernel with the median heuristic: compute the median squared Euclidean distance between a random subset of up to 500 training descriptor rows (using the seed to pick them), and set gamma = 1 / median_sq_dist. Also try a bandwidth multiplier in {0.5, 1, 2} and choose the one whose kernel gives the highest mean kernel-target alignment on the training set (cheap closed-form computation with the rank-normalized target). Keep the Tanimoto mix and SVR head unchanged.
backlog.title: Automatic-metric bandwidth for the descriptor RBF kernel

backlog.spec: Replace the SVR head with a kernel expansion f(x) = K(x, X_train) @ alpha trained by full-batch Adam (learning rate 0.05 with cosine decay to 0 over 1500 steps, initialized at alpha = 0). The loss is squared error against the standardized rank target plus an RKHS penalty lambda * alpha^T K alpha with lambda=0.01. Hold out 15% of training molecules, grouped by Murcko scaffold, as a validation set; keep the alpha with the lowest validation loss as the schedule proceeds, then refit on all training molecules for the same number of steps that gave the best validation loss. Use the existing mixed kernel K. The point is a gradient-based solver with a learned stopping time instead of the SVR dual.
backlog.title: Full-batch Adam on kernel expansion with early stopping

backlog.spec: Fit sklearn ARDRegression (default priors, max_iter=300) on the standardized, clipped RDKit descriptors using the rank-normalized training target. Predict the test set. Convert the ARD predictions and the mixed-kernel SVR predictions to ranks on the test set, and output 0.7 times the SVR rank plus 0.3 times the ARD rank. ARD learns a per-feature precision, so it switches off irrelevant descriptors automatically, a different regularization from the Gaussian-kernel ridge prior already tried. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: ARD Bayesian regression on descriptors as a rank-averaged ensemble member

backlog.spec: Build an ensemble of 8 descriptor RBF kernels, where each kernel is computed on a random 50% of the standardized descriptor columns (chosen with the seed for each member, using the training fold only). For each member, compute the RBF kernel with gamma = 2 / (number of kept columns). Average these 8 kernels and mix equally with the Morgan Tanimoto kernel. Fit the unchanged SVR head. This is random feature dropout applied to the kernel input, a regularizer that is different from random subspace ensembles of SVR outputs already tried.
backlog.title: Feature-level random dropout inside the descriptor kernel
